title: The Third Melphiro
paragraphs: “Huh?”
Is Big Sister turning into a Beastman?
“The Raph that Gaelion knew couldn’t do that. Is this another discovery?”
“It looks like we’re about to find out some unpleasant truths…”
“Why don’t you give it a try?”
Father seems a little excited, or so it seems to me. Or is it just my imagination? Still, it’s rare to see him like this.
“I don’t want to try it.”
“Now, now. Well then, Big Sister will teach you how, so let’s practice a little.”
“Kou can transform, too—you do it like this—poof!”
Kou alternates between his Filolial form and his angel form to demonstrate.
“Just like Filo, you’re terrible at teaching, aren’t you?”

In a similar vein to how Panda taught Keel how to turn into a dog, Big Sister’s older sister taught Big Sister the Beastman transformation technique. Then, with a “pop”… Big Sister transformed into a Beastman form that closely resembled a Raph.
“Oh?”
“Whoa…”
Big Sister’s older sister and Kou each muttered a word. My father-in-law was staring intently at Big Sister.
“Raph.”
Silence reigned all around. Even Éclair and the old woman, who had just received a Class Up and were chatting casually, shifted their gaze to focus on Big Sister.
“W-what’s going on? I mean, this hand…”
Without a word, my father-in-law held up his shield—which reflected like a mirror—to show Big Sister her reflection.
“W-what on earth is thisaaaaaaaaaa!?”
Big Sister screamed.
“This is a surprise. When you mix ‘Raph’ with ‘Raph’s Limit Break,’ you get ‘Raph.’”
“Rival, you should explain it more clearly.”
It certainly is a surprise. So there’s a loop where Big Sister takes on this form. No… since Big Sister was in her Raph form when I escaped the loop, I suppose this is just another possibility.

“What are you so calmly analyzing for?! If it weren’t for you guys creating Raph-chan in the first place, none of this would have happened! I’ve been thinking this for a while now, but just because you’ve been looping and know about Lord Naofumi doesn’t mean there aren’t limits to what you can get away with—”
Just as my Big Sister was confronting me and my Rival, my Father slipped around behind her, grabbed her under the arms, and lifted her up.
“Hmm…”
“Father Naofumi?”
Father started walking while still holding Big Sister aloft.

“Father Naofumi? Where are you taking me? Father Naofumi!? Father 
“Raph.”
The Raph-type, who had gotten off my Father’s back without me noticing, hopped onto Kou’s head and waved at the two of them.
“Kou, I know—Iwatani was saying, while petting Raph, that he wished Raph would look like this.”
“C-Come to think of it, the Wild Naofumi from the first world did say she wanted to pet Raph all over when he looked like this.”
“He did say that.”
“Oh my… Naofumi-chan has a cute side after all.”
I see. So, from Father’s perspective, that form is the ideal way for him to dote on Big Sister.

A little while later, Big Sister looked like she wasn’t entirely displeased. And she didn’t give us any particular warnings. Something good must have happened. She had a somewhat complicated expression, but she wasn’t looking upset.

A little while later, Big Sister was chosen as one of the Seven Star Weapons of the Hammer. Our combat strength has been bolstered. However, it was striking that when she received the Seven Star Weapon of the Hammer, she muttered, “I do wish I’d gotten this before breaking through my limits.”
One day, during a peaceful dinner.
“Gaelion, it’s about time you went and brought peace to that world, isn’t it?”

Rival made this suggestion to my Father during a joyful family gathering in the village. Big Sister, being doted on by my Father with a very gentle smile, didn’t seem to mind at all and was focusing on her meal. It was a scene that looked just like a parent doting on a child.
“That world?”
“It’s the world where Gaelion’s knowledge as the Dragon Emperor originated. You’d understand if I said it’s the world where there’s a possessor of the ‘Glass’ fan-shaped Vassal Weapon, right?”
“Ah… Glass. I was just thinking we might fight again somewhere… Come to think of it, ‘The Wave’ was that world-fusion phenomenon, wasn’t it?”
My Father had already been explained, through me and my Rival, what the Battle of the Wave was all about.
“Bringing peace to that guy’s world, huh…”
“There’s really no need for conflict in the first place.”
“Come to think of it, you guys are technically stuck in a loop, aren’t you?”
“It’s definitely true that we’re moving between parallel worlds.”
My Father looks at me. I get the feeling he’s feeling a bit sympathetic.
“Are you trying to figure out how to end the loop?”
“That’s part of it, but I’m only doing this because I think it would leave a bad aftertaste otherwise.”
“Aftertaste?”

“It’d take a while to explain, but I think Wild Naofumi—who likes things wild—would prefer a brief summary, so I’ll just say this: the scope of the worlds where the loop is occurring is this world of Naofumi’s and that world over there… kind of like the world that fused with ours through the waves in the first world.”

Huh? Was that how it went? Honestly, I couldn’t care less about Ogi-butan’s world. But as for my Rival… come to think of it, in the first world, I was conducting the Gathering of fragments of the Dragon Emperor from Ogi-butan’s world and fighting against my Rival from that same world.
“Hmm… So you guys can’t go to other parallel worlds either?”
“It seems so. We’ve figured that out from trying to enter them in previous loops—anyone who tries gets rejected.”
“It seems there might be a mystery behind why Motoyasu is looping.”
“Unlike the Spear Hero, who was looping at first, there’s no doubt that parallel worlds actually exist. Yes, Naofumi, who cared for Gaelion, definitely exists.”
Ugh… Rival, don’t talk about my Father! It’s my own foolish fault… Ah… I wonder if the time will ever come when I can thank him…
“So, why did we decide to go to the world on Glass’s side?”

“Over there, too, there are reincarnated people running amok, trying to wreak havoc on the world. If we leave them alone, they’ll run wild. Even if we’re stuck in a loop, you should understand that it leaves a bad taste in your mouth.”
Personally, I don’t really care either way. But… I seem to recall that when we went to Siltvelt, my Father heard something along those lines and was investigating it.
“Well… since this is a ‘world fusion phenomenon,’ I guess that guy Glass didn’t exactly come here willingly to fight us.”
“Exactly. While you’re at it, try to work things out with Glass to some extent and negotiate so they don’t end up fighting.”
“I see.”
My Father turns his gaze toward the Assistant. The Assistant, meeting their gaze, furrows his brow in a troubled manner.
“Why not just let Gaelion do as he pleases? He’s incredibly strong, after all…”
The assistant seems to have given up entirely and is now watching the Rival walk away.
“Big sister, you should study hard in the village. That’s what Dad wants, too.”
“Yeah, yeah.”
“Big sister, since you’ve been such a good girl, I’ll let you meet Dad. I want you to spend Gaelion’s absence with him.”
“It’s just some guy from another world, anyway.”
The assistant says to the Rival, sounding irritated.
“No, that’s not it. It’s your big sister’s dad!”
With a click, the Rival pulls out a fragment of the Dragon Emperor and hands it to the Assistant.
“This is the Dragon Emperor fragment that Naofumi obtained in this world, and your dad is inhabiting it. As long as the Dragon Emperor has a body, he can inherit his memories and personality.”
The Assistant gulps, staring at the fragment.

“I thought about having him inhabit my younger brother, who was the Dragon Emperor in the first world, but his personality had become a bit of a hassle, so I think it’s better to keep them separate. We’ll just buy an egg at the market later and have him inhabit it—that’ll bring Dad back to life.”
“Raph.”
The Raph creature clinging to my Father chirps in the exact same tone as Rival’s “na-no.” It’s mimicking her, isn’t it?

“By the way, big sis, Dad’s plan is for you to step into the public eye… Even if he’s revived, he’ll try to play dumb. Don’t give him a chance to say no—show him right here that you’ve grown up into a fine young woman and make sure he doesn’t slip away.”
“U-un…”

“Otherwise, just like when the Spear Hero found out he’d actually been revived in the first world, he’ll run away from you and go into hiding. Well, my little brother was partly to blame for that, too.”

“He’s such a weirdo—he could’ve just changed his body instead of switching genders,” the Rival mutters, referring to the Rival from the first world. He certainly was a strange one, wasn’t he? He stubbornly would only cry out “Cure, Cure.”
“Oh, by the way, I’ll leave some shards behind, so Naofumi, you can rest easy.”
“Is that really okay?”
“I hate humans, but I know my place. Since I’m the self-proclaimed Weakest Dragon Emperor, that means I know my limits.”
And so, after dropping a massive spoiler, my Rival set off. After the battle on the wave Rival had specified, he entered the crack in the wave.
And then, just as I returned to the village… my Assistant came to see my Father.
“Gaelion handed me this Core Stone before he left, and he gave me this…”
There was the compact that he’d given to Filo-tan and my Finacée. Why does even the Assistant have one? Rival, what are you up to?

“That’s the same one Filo and Melty got… So you’re the third Melphilo. Already a second season… no, a revival. Going so far as to have an additional warrior—you really go all out… or rather, you’re even using your own sister as material.”
“I don’t really need it, though…”
“In terms of the concept, I guess those two are like ‘Merphilo☆Dragon Heart’? That’s a total rip-off. So that makes you… ‘The Third Merphilo: Saint Windy!’ Or something like that?”
“Why? Where’d that name come from?”
“…I just borrowed part of your name, didn’t I? And I added ‘Saint’ to make it sound righteous.”
“If Gaelion were here, that’d be a sure thing! Seriously, stop it!”
The assistant is protesting to her Father.
“Good thing she’s not here. Well, apparently the performance itself is pretty good. Should we have Raphtalia make one for us in earnest?”
“Please stop dragging me into this. Naofumi-sama, what do you plan to do with me in the first place?”
“Well, to use Raphtalia at any time without using the Slave Mark—oops, that’d make me sound like a character from *Metal Hero*, controlled by an enemy who’ll eventually become an ally.”
“I absolutely won’t let you make one! Even if you do, I’ll destroy it! No, I’ll make this hammer reject it!”

Big Sister is protesting to Father. But he’s just ruffling her hair and doesn’t seem to be listening. By the way, Big Sister is in her Beastman form. Also, since she’s already been chosen as a Seven Star Weapon, she doesn’t have a Slave Mark.
“Well, why don’t you just try transforming, just in case?”
“No way. Why do I have to become like Filo-chan or Melty-san?”
“Well, I guess he was worried about his sister in his own way? It’d be fine just to keep it as a little trinket—a hand mirror you can use when you’re in a pinch.”
“Hmm…”
The assistant opens the compact. Then…
‘Hmm…’
It sounds like a voice is coming from it.
“W-where am I…!?”
“Huh? What is this compact—it talks? That’s pretty high-tech.”
“Gaelion… you’ve got some weird stuff stashed in here, haven’t you? Is it so I won’t throw it away?”
“Y-yes. I-I am the Transformation Compact Gyaa! My owner is Wyndia. Don’t worry about pointless transformations—I’ll be watching over you, Gyaa!”
“The transformation compact is saying there’s no need to transform. That’s pretty novel.”
Though the voice does sound a bit high-pitched, that way of ending sentences… it reminds me of someone, for some reason.
“Well, as long as you do a great job while the decoder’s away—just like you promised—it’ll bring my parents back, right? Might as well give it a shot… just for a bit of fun.”
“I hate this with every fiber of my being… but if they say they’ll let me see my dad, I guess I have no choice but to do my best…”
“Well, when that guy gets back, I’ll cover for you and say you were doing your best. Just coordinate with Melty and Filo and carry on with your activities.”
“Learning about the human world is more important, Gyaa! Leave the fighting to the heroes, Gyaa!”
The talking compact is giving the Assistant a talking-to. It seems this little guy has a different way of thinking than Rival.
“That was my plan all along… but just in case, I’m trying to learn a little bit about how to fight, too…”
“Gyaa! Avoid pointless battles, gyaa!”
“You’re pretty sensible for a creation of the Decoder. So, Compact, what’s your name?”
Instantly, Compact fell silent.
“Well, ‘Compact’ will do, I suppose.”
Refusing to give your name in front of your Father leads to situations like this. After all, even my Assistant used to call her Taniko when Rival didn’t introduce her.
‘C-Call me Jack, Gyaa!’
Shield…100%　Fallen Raph
